chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with them) narrated what they said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris both narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Hashim, from Dawud ibn Muhammad al-Nahdi, from one of our companions, who said: Ibn Abi Sa'id al-Mukari entered upon al-Rida (peace be upon him).

He said to him, 'May God grant you according to your stature that you claim what your father claimed.' He said to him, 'What is wrong with you? May God extinguish your light and bring poverty into your house. Do you not know that God, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Imran (peace be upon him), 'I will grant you a son'? So He granted him Mary, and He granted Mary Jesus (peace be upon him). Thus Jesus is from Mary, and Mary is from Jesus, and Jesus and Mary (peace be upon them) are one thing. And I am from my father, and my father is from me, and I and my father are one thing.'
Ibn Abi Sa'id said to him, 'Then let me ask you a question.' He said, 'I do not think you will accept from me, for you are not one of my flock, but come with it.'
A man said, 'At the time of his death, he said: Every slave of mine who is 'old' is free for the sake of God, the Mighty and Majestic.'
He said, 'Yes. Indeed, God, Blessed and Exalted, says in His Book,
till he returns like the old (and withered) lower part of a date-stalk.

So whatever of his slaves had been with him for six months, he is considered 'old' and free.' He said, 'So the man left and became poor until he died, and he did not have enough for a night's lodging. May God curse him.'

key_terms.الْعُرْجُونِ الْقَدِيمِ: The old date-stalk, a Quranic metaphor for old age
key_terms.عِمْرَانُ: Imran, father of Mary (mother of Jesus)

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Rida define the concept of 'old' slaves in the context of manumission using Quranic exegesis?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) employs the theological concept of *wahdat al-dhat* (unity of essence) in lineage, drawing a parallel between the unique spiritual bond of Jesus and Mary and the inseparable connection between himself and his father, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS). In the subsequent legal ruling, he interprets the Quranic phrase 'like an old date-stalk' (Al-Baqarah 2:265) to define 'old' (*qadim*) as a slave who has served for six months, thereby granting freedom upon the owner's death. This incident highlights the Imam's mastery of both metaphysical theology and precise jurisprudential interpretation (*ijtihad*) from the Quranic text.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-66 My father and Muhammad ibn Al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Waleed - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash’ari, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Hashem, on the authority of Dawood ibn Muhammad al-Hindi, on the authority of a companion that a man named Abi Sa’eed al-Mukari went to see Al-Ridha (s)

and rudely asked, “Have you reached the point at which you claim to be what your father also claimed to be?” The Imam (s) told him, “None of your business! May God darken your life and make you poor. Don’t you know that the Honorable the Exalted God revealed to Imran (s) that He would grant him a son, but first gave him (the Blessed Baby) Mary (s) and then gave Jesus (s) to (the Blessed Lady) Mary (s)? Thus Jesus (s) and Mary (s) are two different people, but they are one and the same thing. I am from my father (s), and my father (s) is from me. My father (s) and I are also one and the samething.”
Abi Sa’eed said, “Then let me ask you a question.” The Imam (s) said, “I do not think that you will accept my answer. You are not one of my friends or followers. However, ask anyways.”
Abi Sa’eed said, “Consider someone makes a will at the time of his death and says that all his old slaves should be freed. Which of his slaves should be freed?”
The Imam (s) said, “Yes. The Blessed the Sublime God says the following in His Book,
‘…till she returns like the old (and withered) lower part of a date-stalk.’

Therefore, whoever has been a slave for more than six months is considered an old slave and should be freed.”The narrator added, “The man left there and became poor. He was poor until he died. He did not even have enough bread to eat at night. May God damn him!”
